CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys in patient with Smith-Magenis syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old girl born at 34 weeks 3 days gestation as a twin with a birth weight of 4 pounds 8 ounces. She was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis syndrome by neurology. At birth, she experienced feeding difficulties with apneic episodes during feeds and had difficulty with temperature regulation. She did not walk or sit independently by one year of age but is now crawling and attempting to take steps. She is enrolled in multiple therapeutic programs including feeding therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and will be starting speech therapy within the next couple of weeks. She has been evaluated by specialists including neurology, gastroenterology, allergology, orthopedics, ophthalmology, and audiology. She has significant reflux and was removed from cow's milk per dietician recommendation. She currently drinks ripple pea protein milk, water, and occasionally water with juice. She has approximately 8-10 wet diapers per 24 hours and appears to have good fluid intake. Her healthy twin sister is thriving with no health concerns. Patient's older brother is age 9 with autism. The family was counseled that Smith-Magenis syndrome can be associated with congenital kidney and urinary tract anomalies, prompting today's visit for kidney screening.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Significant for reflux, history of feeding difficulties, and developmental delay. Currently no respiratory complaints, adequate urine output, and good fluid intake. Twin sister without symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis syndrome, prematurity at 34 weeks 3 days gestation, gastroesophageal reflux disease, developmental delay, cow's milk intolerance.

MEDICATIONS
Not documented.

ALLERGIES
Cow's milk (intolerance requiring dietary modification).

FAMILY HISTORY
Older brother age 9 with autism. Twin sister without Smith-Magenis syndrome or health problems. No family history of kidney disease, dialysis, or transplant.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives in Dallas, Georgia. Twin birth. Older sibling in home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy when examined. Eyes small appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia. Heart and lungs normal. Ears normal on examination.

RESULTS
Pending kidney ultrasound.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
22-month-old former 34 weeks 3 days gestation, twin with Smith-Magenis syndrome. This chromosomal deletion syndrome can be associated with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. Plan to obtain screening kidney ultrasound today. If abnormalities are identified on ultrasound, will determine next steps and future follow-up. If ultrasound is normal, no further follow-up needed at this time. Patient's family lives in Dallas, Georgia; follow-up if needed should be coordinated at town center location.
